message:
## Vulnerability Digest

Eleven relevant advisory groups were newly reported or surfaced during the last 24 hours. The highest-priority items are critical PHP remote-code-execution flaws affecting Ubuntu packages, critical Chrome memory-corruption fixes, high-severity Node.js issues, and a high-severity MongoDB Compass code-execution flaw.

**Scope:** `Products.txt` and `List_of_SIA_Completed.txt` only, combined and deduplicated. The DLL component source was not read or combined.

**Scan window:** 2026-10-20 23:40 UTC through 2026-10-21 23:40 UTC (2026-10-21 05:10 IST through 2026-10-22 05:10 IST).

### Finding 1: PHP remote code execution in Ubuntu

- **Affected product/component:** Ubuntu PHP packages
- **Issue:** CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619; USN-8948-1 and USN-8948-2
- **Severity:** Critical (Ubuntu)
- **Description:** Crafted network requests can trigger unsafe request-state and memory handling, allowing an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code.
- **Relevance:** Ubuntu is monitored, and Canonical published fixes for supported and ESM Ubuntu releases.
- **Source:** [Ubuntu USN-8948-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8948-1)

### Finding 2: Google Chrome 156 security release

- **Affected product/component:** Google Chrome for desktop
- **Issue:** Chrome 156 security update, including six listed Critical CVEs such as CVE-2026-113341, CVE-2026-113279, CVE-2026-113072, CVE-2026-113280, CVE-2026-113271, and CVE-2026-113303
- **Severity:** Critical and High issues are present
- **Description:** Chrome 156.0.8078.47/.48 addresses 353 security fixes, including multiple memory-corruption and use-after-free flaws.
- **Relevance:** Google Chrome is explicitly monitored; a government advisory surfaced the update on October 21.
- **Source:** [Chrome Releases](https://chromereleases.googleblog.com/2026/10/stable-channel-update-for-desktop_02018666648.html)

### Finding 3: Node.js October security release

- **Affected product/component:** Node.js 22.x, 24.x, and 26.x
- **Issue:** CVE-2026-105482, CVE-2026-105483, CVE-2026-106069, CVE-2026-111497, CVE-2026-105481, CVE-2026-106072, CVE-2026-106074, CVE-2026-106070, CVE-2026-106071, and CVE-2026-106073
- **Severity:** Four High, three Medium, and three Low
- **Description:** The release fixes DNS truncation, TLS hostname-validation bypasses, Brotli decoder remote code execution, repeated random values in snapshots, and permission-model or ZIP-handling weaknesses.
- **Relevance:** Node.js is explicitly monitored, and the advisory directly names affected release lines.
- **Source:** [Node.js security release](https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/october-2026-security-releases)

### Finding 4: MongoDB Compass arbitrary code execution

- **Affected product/component:** MongoDB Compass 1.7.0 through versions before 1.49.15
- **Issue:** CVE-2026-113870
- **Severity:** High, CVSS 8.8
- **Description:** A crafted stored view can exploit improper BSON-value escaping when opened for editing, causing code execution with the Compass user's privileges.
- **Relevance:** MongoDB is monitored, and Compass is an official MongoDB ecosystem component covered by the mandatory sweep.
- **Source:** [MongoDB Compass release notes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/compass/release-notes/), [CVE record summary](https://radar.offseq.com/threat/cve-2026-113870-cwe-116-improper-encoding-or-escaping-of-output-in-mongodb-compass-f723b5ac6c2861e7)

### Finding 5: SolarWinds Observability Self-Hosted authorization bypass

- **Affected product/component:** SolarWinds Observability Self-Hosted before 2026.4
- **Issue:** CVE-2026-28328
- **Severity:** High, CVSS 8.8
- **Description:** A low-privileged authenticated user can access or modify information outside the permissions assigned to that account.
- **Relevance:** SolarWinds is explicitly monitored; the Canadian Cyber Centre issued an in-window advisory.
- **Source:** [Canadian Centre for Cyber Security AV26-1068](https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/alerts-advisories/solarwinds-security-advisory-av26-1068)

### Finding 6: Firefox and Firefox ESR security updates

- **Affected product/component:** Firefox before 158.0.1; Firefox ESR before 153.5.1 or 115.43.1
- **Issue:** MFSA 2026-111 through MFSA 2026-113; CVE-2026-113399, CVE-2026-113470, CVE-2026-113400, and CVE-2026-113401
- **Severity:** Overall High; individual issues range from High to Low
- **Description:** The updates address SVG boundary handling, a compromised-certificate block-list issue, uninitialized media memory, and PDF-viewer denial of service.
- **Relevance:** Mozilla Firefox is explicitly monitored; CERT-FR published an in-window notice covering the vendor advisories.
- **Source:** [Mozilla MFSA 2026-111](https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/security/advisories/mfsa2026-111/), [CERT-FR notice](https://www.cert.cyber.gouv.fr/avis/CERTFR-2026-AVI-1346/)

### Finding 7: Thunderbird security updates

- **Affected product/component:** Thunderbird before 158.0.1 or 153.5.1
- **Issue:** MFSA 2026-114 and MFSA 2026-115; CVE-2026-113866 through CVE-2026-113869, plus shared Mozilla component CVEs
- **Severity:** Overall High
- **Description:** Flaws include Exchange credentials sent over HTTP during setup, XMPP stanza injection, NTLM memory disclosure/crash conditions, and an S/MIME use-after-free.
- **Relevance:** Mozilla Thunderbird appears in the approved-software list.
- **Source:** [Mozilla MFSA 2026-114](https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/security/advisories/mfsa2026-114/)

### Finding 8: Ubuntu Ghostscript memory-safety flaws

- **Affected product/component:** Ubuntu Ghostscript packages
- **Issue:** CVE-2026-101258, CVE-2026-103226, and one issue without a CVE
- **Severity:** Not clearly stated in the Ubuntu notice
- **Description:** Crafted PostScript or font files may bypass the sandbox, crash Ghostscript, or execute arbitrary code.
- **Relevance:** Ubuntu is monitored, and Canonical published fixes for Ubuntu 16.04 through 26.10.
- **Source:** [Ubuntu USN-8949-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8949-1)

### Finding 9: Ubuntu Poppler denial of service

- **Affected product/component:** Ubuntu Poppler PDF-rendering packages
- **Issue:** CVE-2026-107705
- **Severity:** Not clearly stated in the Ubuntu notice
- **Description:** A specially crafted encrypted PDF can trigger incorrect password-length handling and crash the renderer.
- **Relevance:** Ubuntu is monitored, and affected packages are present in Ubuntu 22.04 through 26.10.
- **Source:** [Ubuntu USN-8950-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8950-1)

### Finding 10: Ubuntu U-Boot memory-safety flaws

- **Affected product/component:** U-Boot on Ubuntu 26.10
- **Issue:** CVE-2026-74220, CVE-2026-74221, CVE-2026-74222, and CVE-2026-74225
- **Severity:** Not clearly stated in the Ubuntu notice
- **Description:** Malformed NFS, HTTP, or DHCPv6 data may cause buffer overflows, use-after-free, denial of service, or arbitrary code execution during network boot.
- **Relevance:** Ubuntu is monitored; this notice applies specifically to Ubuntu 26.10 packages.
- **Source:** [Ubuntu USN-8930-2](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8930-2)

### Finding 11: Ubuntu Unbound DNS vulnerabilities

- **Affected product/component:** Unbound packages on Ubuntu 14.04 through 26.04
- **Issue:** USN-8946-1; ten CVEs including CVE-2026-80225, CVE-2026-81634, CVE-2026-85501, CVE-2026-44690, and CVE-2026-32665
- **Severity:** Not clearly stated in the Ubuntu notice
- **Description:** Multiple DNS, DNSSEC, DNSCrypt, and DNS-over-QUIC handling flaws can cause denial of service; one issue can poison cached DNS responses.
- **Relevance:** Ubuntu is monitored, and Canonical directly identifies affected Ubuntu releases.
- **Source:** [Ubuntu USN-8946-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8946-1)

### MongoDB ecosystem verification

The mandatory sweep checked MongoDB Server Community and Enterprise, `mongod`, `mongos`, Atlas and Atlas services, Ops Manager, Cloud Manager, Compass, `mongosh`, Database Tools, Kubernetes Operator, drivers, connectors, BI Connector, Charts, Realm/App Services, official integrations and maintained libraries, MongoDB-owned notices, CVE/NVD-style records, GitHub advisories, and CISA sources. Only CVE-2026-113870 for MongoDB Compass was newly disclosed in the scan window; no other credible MongoDB-family finding was new or materially updated.

### Review priority

Immediate review is recommended for exposed Ubuntu PHP workloads, Chrome endpoints, affected Node.js runtimes, and MongoDB Compass installations. SolarWinds, Firefox, Thunderbird, and the remaining Ubuntu package updates should follow promptly based on deployed versions and exposure.
